R5A-bear-atv-0001.name: 130 m NE of Boss Creek
R5A-bear-atv-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5A-bear-atv-0001.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (unnamed paved road); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2019 (7 years old), 480 m N: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 20 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Boss Creek 130 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: Bag 2; parts of MU 5-9 are closed to black bear hunting (Map F14, page 52) and the Mussel Inlet Special Management Area in MU 5-9 has no black bear season (page 43)

plan: Drive: from Old Bella Bella, about 124 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.39572, -127.48045, where the truck road ends (unnamed paved road); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 5.3 km on unnamed roads and trails by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 80 m SW, climb about 24 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-7, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-07, closures 2026-10-16.

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.1 km and about 24 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

plan: Drive: from Old Bella Bella, about 110 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.49038, -127.51894, pull off on Johnston M/L (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk or drive slowly: the Johnston M/L stretch, 4.3 km one way. About 87 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
